summary: All requested checks PASS for the password-gated Trigger Earthquake Alert feature. Legacy /api/status GET+POST unchanged (no gate). FRONTEND code: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx no longer imports or calls broadcastAlert (grep count=0), comment at L160-163 documents mobile is local-test-only. push.ts registerForPushNotifications unchanged. critical_code_review_comments: server.py L142-147: fail-closed guard (500 when ADMIN_TRIGGER_PASSWORD empty, 401 when header mismatches) is correct and safe — prevents anonymous triggers if operator forgets to set the env var.

server.py L192: CORS allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True is technically a spec violation (browsers ignore * when credentials=true), but since the dashboard fetch does not send cookies (only X-Admin-Token header), this works fine in practice. Consider tightening to explicit safequake origin(s) later if credentials are ever added.

server.py L80-89: db.push_devices upsert happens BEFORE the upstream Emergent push relay call — good pattern; ensures local recipient list is authoritative even when upstream is misconfigured (verified by test_register_push_writes_local_db_even_when_upstream_fails).

index.tsx L64-177 handleTrigger: broadcastAlert import + call removed cleanly; the comment L160-163 clearly documents that mobile trigger is local-only and directs to the dashboard button — matches spec.
push.ts still exports broadcastAlert (unused). Safe to keep as an API for future dashboard tooling; not a bug. Left as-is since not requested to remove.

dashboard-trigger-button.html: QUAKEGUARD_BACKEND is currently hardcoded to https://quake-alert-18.emergent.host per the inline instructions; that's the intended deploy target for the safequake dashboard. window.confirm before window.prompt gives a double-confirm UX which is appropriate for a broadcast action.

Register-push writes to db.push_devices even when Emergent relay returns 401 (placeholder key), so recipients count is accurate locally. CORS preflight accepts x-admin-token header from any origin (allow_origins=['*']). Future work: consider narrowing CORS to safequake.onrender.com only if credentials are ever needed.
